text:
Marathon's stock dipped slightly today after a volatile week that saw it surge nearly 13% over two weeks. The immediate driver appears to be profit-taking following yesterday's sharp 1.6% gain to $484.92, which came as oil prices spiked on Iran's escalating attacks in the Strait of Hormuz—a critical shipping chokepoint for roughly 20% of global oil. With Brent crude touching $110 and U.S. crude at $101.91, refiners benefit from the wider spread between crude costs and product prices, but that same volatility can prompt traders to lock in gains.

The underlying strength in the stock reflects real tailwinds for Marathon as a refiner. U.S. refineries are running at 93.5% capacity amid tight diesel supplies (as evidenced by the surge in shipping costs and international focus on diesel-rich refineries), while oil inventories remain relatively lean at 698 million barrels. These conditions favor margin expansion for refiners, even as geopolitical risk keeps oil prices elevated—the physical cost of moving crude has climbed roughly $38 per barrel due to tanker rate spikes, squeezing some competitors but benefiting those with reliable supply chains.
